description: GUI that lists the PowerShell scripts of a folder, reads their built-in help and builds the command line for you
pre_install: if (-not (Test-Path "$dir\Show-PSScriptLauncher.ps1") -or -not (Test-Path "$dir\PSScriptLauncher\PSScriptLauncher.psm1")) { abort 'PSScriptLauncher layout changed upstream: update the pre_install keep list.' }

Set-Content "$dir\PSScriptLauncher.cmd" ('@echo off', 'set "ps=powershell.exe"', 'where pwsh.exe >nul 2>nul && set "ps=pwsh.exe"', '"%ps%" -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -WindowStyle Hidden -File "%~dp0Show-PSScriptLauncher.ps1" %*') -Encoding Ascii
notes: Run 'psscriptlauncher' to open the window and pick the folder with the Folder... button or Ctrl+O, or 'psscriptlauncher -Path <folder>' to start on another folder.

The Start Menu shortcut runs PowerShell 7 when it is installed, otherwise Windows PowerShell 5.1; 'psscriptlauncher' runs in the PowerShell session you call it from and needs an execution policy that allows local scripts (RemoteSigned or Bypass).
